subline

Read what your friends are actually saying.

It drops a translation under any Discord message in a language you don't read. Same Discord, same account — nothing new to open, nothing to sign up for.

Installing

About that warning

The builds aren't code-signed yet — I haven't paid for a certificate. So your computer warns you once. It means "unverified," not "unsafe." Here's the click-through.

  1. Drag Subline to Applications.

    From the .dmg you downloaded.

  2. Right-click Subline → Open.

    macOS saysApple could not verify "Subline" is free of malware…

    Right-click, not double-click. That gives you an Open button the double-click doesn't.

  3. Still stuck? Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.

    Confirm with your password. Once, for this app, done.

  1. Run Subline-Setup.exe.

    Windows saysWindows protected your PC.

    More info → Run anyway. That's the whole trick.

  2. Click Install.

    It closes Discord, patches it, reopens it. You're done.

Privacy

Where your messages go

Translating means sending text somewhere. Here's exactly where — I'd rather you pass on Subline knowing this than install it not knowing.

WhatGoes whereStored?
Message textGoogle for the instant line. The AI you pick (Groq, Gemini or Claude) for the sharper one, only if you add a key.Not by me. No server, nothing saved.
Who sent itNowhere. Names, avatars, servers — never sent.—
Your API keyStays on your machine, in Discord's own settings. Goes only to your AI, only when you translate.Your machine.
Usage dataNone. No analytics, no tracking, nothing.—
  • off
    DMs stay private. Never translated unless you turn one on, per conversation.
  • off
    Your own language never leaves. Subline checks on your machine first and skips it.
  • you
    Kill it per channel. Nothing leaves a channel you've switched off.
